help.intro: The possessives for more than one owner, and the formal one: unser (our), euer (your — several friends), ihr (their) and Ihr with a capital (your — formal, one person or several). They work exactly like mein: they take the ein-endings, decided by the noun that follows — unser Sohn, unsere Tochter, unsere Kinder, and in the accusative unseren Sohn. Two details make them tricky. euer loses its second e as soon as an ending is added: euer Hund, but eure Katze, euren Hund. And ihr / Ihr is the same word in speech: in writing the capital decides between 'their' and 'your (formal)', and in speech the situation does — Herr Braun, ist das Ihr Koffer? The quiz gives you the owner in brackets; choose the word and add the ending for the noun.
help.tips[0].title: Owner first
help.tips[0].text: wir → unser · ihr (you all) → euer · sie (they) → ihr · Sie → Ihr. Then the ending comes from the noun, as with mein.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: Tom and Lisa are selling their flat.
help.tips[0].check.q: Wir haben ein Auto. Das ist ____ Auto.
help.tips[0].check.why: The owner is wir, so the possessive is unser. euer belongs to ihr (you all), ihr to sie (they).
help.tips[0].visual.columns[0].label: owner word
help.tips[1].title: The endings: nothing, -e, -en
help.tips[1].text: der/das-noun (nominative): no ending — unser Sohn, euer Auto. die-noun and plural: -e — unsere Tochter, eure Kinder. der-noun as an object: -en — unseren Garten, euren Schlüssel.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: Our children are playing in the garden.
help.tips[1].check.why: Großvater is masculine and the object of besuchen, so the ending is -en: unseren.
help.tips[2].title: euer drops an e
help.tips[2].text: euer + ending = eur-: eure Lehrerin, euren Hund. unser keeps both e’s: unsere, unseren.
help.tips[2].trap: 'euere' and 'euern' look logical but are not the standard forms; write eure, euren.
help.tips[2].check.why: Plural nouns take -e, and euer drops its second e when an ending is added: eure.
help.tips[3].title: Ihr with a capital = your (formal)
help.tips[3].text: Talking to someone you call Sie, the possessive is Ihr / Ihre / Ihren — capital I, like Sie.
help.tips[3].examples[0].en: Mr Braun, is that your suitcase?
help.tips[3].examples[1].en: Mrs Weber, what's your phone number?
help.tips[3].check.q: Herr Lang, wo wohnen ____ Eltern? (you say Sie to him)
help.tips[3].check.why: For someone you call Sie, 'your' is Ihr with a capital; Eltern is plural, so it takes -e: Ihre.
help.remember[0]: unser – euer – ihr – Ihr: our, your (all), their, your (formal).
help.remember[1]: euer + ending loses an e: eure, euren.
help.context.en: This is our house, and this is our garden. Our children often play here. And you? What's your flat like? Have you finished your balcony yet? – Yes! And Mrs Klein, is that your dog? – No, that's Tom and Lisa's dog. Their dog is called Bello.
help.mistakes[0].why: Tochter is a die-noun, so the possessive takes -e.
help.mistakes[1].why: Opa is a der-noun and the object: -en.
help.mistakes[2].why: Formal your is written with a capital I.
help.hook: Our house, your flat, their dog: with unser, euer and ihr you can talk about things that belong to more than one person.
sentences[0].english: That's our house. We've lived here for two years.
sentences[0].why: 'Our' is unser — no ending before a das-word in the nominative.
sentences[1].why: 'Your' (you all) is euer, and before a die-word it drops its inner e: eure.
sentences[2].english: Mr Braun, is that your suitcase?
sentences[2].why: Formal 'your' is Ihr, capital I — no ending before the der-word Koffer.
sentences[3].english: Our daughter is ten years old.
sentences[3].why: die Tochter is feminine: unser + -e = Unsere.
sentences[4].english: Is that your car in front of the house?
sentences[4].why: Before the das-word Auto, euer keeps its bare form: euer.
sentences[5].english: Mrs Weber, is that your bag?
sentences[5].why: die Tasche is feminine: formal Ihr + -e = Ihre.
sentences[6].english: Our children are playing in the garden.
sentences[6].why: Kinder is plural, and plurals take -e like die-words: Unsere Kinder.
sentences[7].why: der Hund, nominative: euer stays bare — no ending on a der-word subject.
sentences[8].english: We're visiting our grandma on Sunday.
sentences[8].why: die Oma takes -e: unsere — feminine looks the same as subject or object.
sentences[9].why: der Schlüssel as object: accusative masculine -en, and euer squeezes to eur-: euren.
sentences[10].why: der Garten as object: accusative masculine adds -en — unseren.
sentences[11].english: Can I see your passport, please, Mr Klein?
sentences[11].why: der Pass as object: formal Ihr + -en = Ihren.
sentences[12].why: Eltern is plural: euer + -e, with the inner e dropped — eure.
sentences[13].english: Tom and Lisa are selling their flat.
sentences[13].why: 'Their' is ihr, and die Wohnung asks for -e: ihre — small i, unlike the formal Ihre.
sentences[14].english: Mrs Weber, what's your phone number?
sentences[14].why: die Telefonnummer: formal Ihre with -e and the capital I.
sentences[15].english: The children are looking for their ball.
sentences[15].why: 'Their' ball as object: ihr + accusative masculine -en = ihren.
